To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the kidney recipient's path from the first visit at a transplant center until transplantation is different for living and deceased donor recipients; and 2) there are differences in the time from first contact at the transplant center until transplantation between living and deceased donor kidney recipients, and between different ethnicities.
The path to kidney transplantation was longer and more complex for recipients with a deceased kidney donor than for recipients with a living kidney donor.
the kidney recipient's path from referral to transplantation is longer for living donor recipients than for deceased donor recipients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model for the design of an integrated, multi-disciplinary approach to the management and control of the kidney recipient's path.
the development and evaluation of a novel approach to kidney transplantation.
the study of the kidney recipient's path through the process of renal transplantation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the kidney recipient's path from the decision to be listed for kidney transplantation until the actual transplantation is different for the deceased donor and the living donor recipients.

living donor kidney transplantation has the following advantages over deceased donor transplantation: 1) better long-term graft survival; 2) better long-term patient survival; 3) lower incidence of delayed graft function; 4) better graft function in the early posttransplant period; 5) better graft function at the end of the first year after transplantation; 6) better quality of life; 7) lower risk of death with a functioning graft; and 8) lower cost. 201
